'''Lawrence William Jones''' (November 16, 1925 – June 30, 2023) was an American academic and professor emeritus in the physics department at the [[University of Michigan]]. His field of interest was [[Particle physics|high energy particle physics]].

== Early life and education ==
Lawrence W. Jones was born in [[Evanston, Illinois]], on November 16, 1925.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Congress|first=The Library of|title=LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress)|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/no91022935.html|access-date=2021-03-14|website=id.loc.gov}}</ref><ref name="obit">{{cite web |title=Lawrence W. Jones |url=https://obits.mlive.com/us/obituaries/annarbor/name/lawrence-jones-obituary?id=52396925 |website=Legacy |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref>

His father was C. Herbert Jones, a mathematics teacher at [[New Trier High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1987-04-30 |title=C.H. JONES, LONGTIME TEACHER AT NEW TRIER |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1987/04/30/ch-jones-longtime-teacher-at-new-trier/ |access-date=2024-09-11 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=C. Herbert |title=C. Herbert Jones (1889-1987) oral history |url=https://history.wilmettelibrary.info/details.asp?ID=64058 |access-date=2024-09-11 |website=history.wilmettelibrary.info |language=en}}</ref> Lawrence Jones graduated from New Trier in 1943.<ref>New Trier Township High School - Echoes Yearbook, Winnetka, IL, 1943; pages [http://www.e-yearbook.com/yearbooks/New_Trier_Township_High_School_Echoes_Yearbook/1943/Page_68.html 68] and [http://www.e-yearbook.com/yearbooks/New_Trier_Township_High_School_Echoes_Yearbook/1943/Page_117.html 117].</ref>

Jones entered [[Northwestern University]] in the summer of 1943 and was drafted into the [[U.S. Army]] in February 1944.  He shipped to Europe on the {{ship|RMS|Aquitania}} in December 1944, and served in the [[Signal Corps (United States Army)|Signal Corps]] Company of the [[35th Infantry Division (United States)|35th Infantry Division]] until December 1945, when he returned to the United States on the {{ship|RMS|Queen Mary}}.  Jones returned to Northwestern for the spring term in 1946 and earned a B.S. with a double major in zoology and physics 1948 and an M.S. in 1949.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-03-25 |title=Larry Jones – Recollections of WWII |url=https://michiganphysics.com/history/history-by-year/1937-1957/larry-jones-recollections-of-wwii/ |access-date=2024-09-11 |website=MichiganPhysics |language=en}}</ref> In 1952 he received a Ph.D. at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/b/bhlead/umich-bhl-02138?view=text|title=BHL: Lawrence W. Jones papers 1952-2006|last=|first=|date=|website=quod.lib.umich.edu|publisher=|access-date=2016-07-10}}</ref> He and his wife Ruth married in 1950, and they had three children.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Jones worked his entire career at the University of Michigan, where he joined the physics faculty as an instructor in 1952. He became an assistant professor there in 1956 and associate professor in 1960. He was promoted to professor in 1963, and he served as physics department chair between 1982 and 1987.<ref name=":0" />

With [[Martin Lewis Perl|Martin Perl]], he was dissertation advisor to [[Samuel C. C. Ting]] in 1962.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/1976/ting-bio.html|title=Samuel C.C. Ting - Biographical|website=www.nobelprize.org|access-date=2016-03-06}}</ref>

== Research ==
Jones's research depended on and led to developments in particle accelerators and detectors.<ref name=":0" /> In the 1950s, he collaborated in the [[Midwestern Universities Research Association]], which developed the concept of colliding beams in modern [[particle accelerator]]s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/lawrence-w-jones/memoir|title=Memoir - Faculty History Project |date= |website=The History of University of Michigan, 1817–2017 |publisher=Anne Duderstadt |access-date=2016-07-10 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618015203/http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/lawrence-w-jones/memoir |archive-date=2018-06-18}}</ref> He contributed to development of the scintillation chamber, optical [[spark chamber]], and the ionization [[Calorimeter (particle physics)|calorimeter]] for [[hadron]] energy measurement.<ref name=":1" /> He participated in experiments on hadron cross-sections as well as elastic and inelastic scattering and production of particles, dimuons, [[neutrino]]s, and proton charm production.

In 1983, Jones joined in the [[L3 experiment]] led by his former student, Nobel laureate [[Samuel C.C. Ting]]. He and Michigan colleagues designed and constructed the hadron calorimeter.<ref name=":0" /> He also contributed to research in [[Medical imaging|medical radioisotope imaging]] and was an early proponent of the [[Hydrogen economy|hydrogen fuel economy]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>Leslie Rogers, Lawrence W Jones, William H. Beierwaltes, Imaging In Nuclear Medicine With Incoherent Holography, Conference on Application of Optical Instrumentation in Medicine, May 1972; DOI: 10.1117/12.953674.</ref><ref>{{cite conference |title=Toward a liquid hydrogen fuel economy |last1= Jones |first1=Lawrence W |date= 13 March 1970 |publisher=[[University of Michigan]] |conference= University of Michigan Environmental Action for Survival Teach In |location=Ann Arbor, Michigan |hdl = 2027.42/5800}}</ref>

Regents of the University of Michigan named Jones professor emeritus of physics in 1998.<ref name=":1" />

== Death ==
Jones died in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], on June 30, 2023, at the age of 97.<ref name="obit"/>

== Honors ==
Jones was a [[Ford Foundation|Ford Foundation Fellow]] (1961–1962) and a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] (1964–1965) at [[CERN]] in [[Switzerland]].<ref name=":0" />

== Selected publications ==
With four colleagues, he wrote ''Innovation was not Enough; the History of the Midwestern Universities Research Association (MURA)'', which [[World Scientific]] published in 2009, describing their work researching particle accelerator design between 1950–1960.<ref name="inno">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Bn7Z4VVB9uUC&pg=PP1|title=Innovation was not enough: a history of the Midwestern Universities Research Association (MURA)|last2=Mills|first2=F.|last3=Sessler|first3=A.|last4=Symon|first4=K.|last5=Young|first5=D.|publisher=World Scientific|year=2010|isbn=9789812832832|first1=L.|last1=Jones}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lsa.umich.edu/physics/directory/emeritus/ci.joneslawrence_ci.detail|title=Emeritus - Physics - University of Michigan|website=www.lsa.umich.edu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713122102/https://www.lsa.umich.edu/physics/directory/emeritus/joneslawrence_ci|archive-date=2015-07-13|url-status=dead|access-date=2016-03-06}}</ref>

Jones co-authored 369 publications and solo authored 6 papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/L.W.Jones.1|title=Jones, Lawrence W., (Spokesperson) - Profile - INSPIRE-HEP|website=inspirehep.net|access-date=2016-07-11}}</ref>
